edition: Lenny scripted speech for Fal (Australian female)

speech.text: Hello, explorer! What should I call you? Type your name or nickname, then tap Let’s play.
Oh, hello there! I’m Lenny. Hee hee! Shall we go on a little adventure?
Oh, hello, Banksia! You can go on an adventure, talk to me, or hear a joke. Tap a big button.
Mmm! That was scrumptious! High paws, Banksia!
A little lion hug, Banksia! You found a secret heart. Squeeeze!
All six! A giant lion hug, Banksia! You found a secret heart. Squeeeze!

Can your team find the treasure using words? Our mission is Secret Island Map. Tap Let’s go when you’re ready.
First, get ready. You need Paper, crayons, a small toy and a partner. Tap Next when you’re ready.
With a partner, make an island on paper. Add a start, a treasure and three obstacles. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Choose who gives directions first. Your partner moves a toy along the map, following your words. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Can you guide them to the treasure without touching an obstacle? Give one direction at a time. Tap Next when you’re ready.

Swap jobs. Change any direction that was confusing, then tell each other which words helped. Show your partner the route and explain one direction you improved When you’re ready, show someone what you made or decided.
Which direction did you change to help your partner? You can tell me your idea, or show someone beside you. If it needs another go, that’s what inventors do.

Can you build a picture in someone else’s mind? Our mission is The Secret Builder. Tap Let’s go when you’re ready.
First, get ready. You need Five safe objects, paper, crayons and a partner. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Choose five safe objects. One person makes a little model while the other looks away. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Describe your model to your partner. They draw it without looking. Use words like beside, above and between. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Compare the drawing with the model. Find one detail your words could explain more clearly. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Swap builder and artist. Try your clearer words and see what changes. Compare the drawing with your model and explain one clearer clue When you’re ready, show someone what you made or decided.
What did your partner’s drawing teach you about your clues? You can tell me your idea, or show someone beside you. If it needs another go, that’s what inventors do.

A toy is stranded! Can your team bring it home? Our mission is Rescue Mission. Tap Let’s go when you’re ready.
First, get ready. You need A toy, paper for a river, two cushions, a towel and a partner. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Put a toy beside a paper river on the floor. You have two cushions and a towel to make a safe route. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Make a rescue plan together. Each person adds an idea. Choose who plans the route and who moves the toy. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Try the rescue. Keep your feet on the floor and pretend the toy cannot touch the river. Tap Next when you’re ready.

Swap jobs and try a better route. Tell your partner which idea made the rescue work. Show your team’s rescue and explain which two ideas you used When you’re ready, show someone what you made or decided.
Which two ideas did your team use in the rescue? You can tell me your idea, or show someone beside you. If it needs another go, that’s what inventors do.

One story. Two endings. Which will your audience choose? Our mission is The Wrong Ending. Tap Let’s go when you’re ready.
First, get ready. You need Toys or drawing paper, and someone to hear your story. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Choose a character, a place and something the character wants. Draw them or use toys. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Tell a story with a beginning, a problem and an ending. Act it out for someone. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Now change the ending. What if your character makes a different choice? Tap Next when you’re ready.
Tell both endings. Ask your listener which they prefer and why. Tell both endings and explain which one your audience chose When you’re ready, show someone what you made or decided.
Which ending did your audience choose? Why? You can tell me your idea, or show someone beside you. If it needs another go, that’s what inventors do.

Can you make an ordinary thing sound extraordinary? Our mission is The Mystery Object Show. Tap Let’s go when you’re ready.
First, get ready. You need One safe household object and a willing audience. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Choose a safe object and imagine a new use for it. A sock could be a dragon’s sleeping bag! Tap Next when you’re ready.
Practise a short show. Tell your audience what it is, how it works and who would use it. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Give your show without naming the real object. Let your audience guess. Tap Next when you’re ready.

Listen to their question. Add one detail to make your explanation clearer, then try your show again. Show your invention and explain a detail you added after a question When you’re ready, show someone what you made or decided.
What detail helped your audience understand your invention? You can tell me your idea, or show someone beside you. If it needs another go, that’s what inventors do.

A visitor has landed on Lenny’s island. Get the story! Our mission is Lenny’s Newsroom. Tap Let’s go when you’re ready.
First, get ready. You need A toy and a partner to play the visitor. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Choose a toy to be a visitor from a made-up planet. Ask a partner to be the visitor. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Think of three questions. Find out where they live, what they eat and one surprising fact. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Listen to the answers. Give a short news report about your visitor using all three facts. Tap Next when you’re ready.

Ask the visitor if you got the facts right. Fix one detail and give your report again. Give your report and explain a fact you checked with your visitor When you’re ready, show someone what you made or decided.
Which fact did you fix after checking with your visitor? You can tell me your idea, or show someone beside you. If it needs another go, that’s what inventors do.

First, get ready. You need Paper, crayons, five large paper coins and a customer. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Draw three things to sell. Give them prices of one, two and three paper coins. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Give your customer five paper coins. Explain what makes each thing worth buying. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Let them choose what to buy. Count the cost and how many coins they have left. Tap Next when you’re ready.

Ask why they chose it. Improve one thing in your shop, then swap jobs and try again. Show a purchase, count the coins and explain your customer’s choice When you’re ready, show someone what you made or decided.

First, get ready. You need A toy, paper, a towel or box, and a customer. A grown-up can help with tape. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Ask someone which toy needs a bed, a shelter or a carrying box. Listen to what it must do. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Draw two different ideas. Ask which one they would like you to build and why. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Build their choice using paper, a towel or a box. Ask a grown-up for help if you need tape. Tap Next when you’re ready.

Let your customer test it with the toy. Use their feedback to change one thing, then show what improved. Show your design and explain a change your customer helped you make When you’re ready, show someone what you made or decided.

Plan a pretend party for a toy. Make eight large paper coins. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Draw choices for snacks, games and decorations. Give each choice a price from one to three coins. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Pick things for your party without spending more than eight coins. Count what is left. Tap Next when you’re ready.

A guest wants one more game. Decide what you could swap or remove to pay for it. Explain your choice. Show your eight-coin party plan and explain a choice you gave up When you’re ready, show someone what you made or decided.
What did you give up so you could afford your party? You can tell me your idea, or show someone beside you. If it needs another go, that’s what inventors do.

First, get ready. You need Two toys, one crayon and a partner. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Pretend two toys both want the same special crayon. Ask a partner to speak for one toy. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Each toy explains why it wants the crayon. Listen before you suggest a plan. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Think of two ways to share it. Ask what each toy likes or dislikes about each plan. Tap Next when you’re ready.

Choose a plan together and act it out. If one toy is unhappy, change the plan and try again. Act out your sharing plan and explain why both toys can use it When you’re ready, show someone what you made or decided.
Why did you choose that plan? What might the other toy say? You can tell me your idea, or show someone beside you. If it needs another go, that’s what inventors do.

Imagine a toy is new to a game. Ask a partner to play the new toy. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Ask the newcomer what they like and what they are unsure about. Listen to the answer. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Change one rule or give them a useful role so they can join in. Play a short round. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Ask how it felt to join. Use their answer to make your welcome even better. Show how you changed a game so someone new could join When you’re ready, show someone what you made or decided.

Ask someone at home what small thing would make their day easier. Listen without guessing. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Think of two ways you could help. Ask which would be most useful. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Do the chosen job with their permission. Ask a grown-up to help if you need it. Tap Next when you’re ready.

Ask whether your help worked. Tell Lenny what you noticed and what you would do next time. Show the help you gave and explain how you found out it was useful When you’re ready, show someone what you made or decided.

Can one sheet of paper become a stronger bridge? Our mission is The Paper Bridge Lab. Tap Let’s go when you’re ready.
First, get ready. You need Two low books, one sheet of paper and three paper balls. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Put two low books a hand-width apart. Use one sheet of paper to make a bridge. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Test it with three paper balls. How many stay on before the bridge bends? Tap Next when you’re ready.
Use the same sheet to make a different bridge. Try folds or a rolled edge. Test with the same balls. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Compare your tests. Choose the stronger design and explain what you changed. Show both bridge tests and explain which design worked better When you’re ready, show someone what you made or decided.
What stayed the same in your two tests? What changed? You can tell me your idea, or show someone beside you. If it needs another go, that’s what inventors do.

Build a puzzle that is tricky, fair and fun. Our mission is Make a Marble-Free Maze. Tap Let’s go when you’re ready.
First, get ready. You need Paper, crayons, one large paper ball and a tester. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Draw a maze for a large paper ball. Add a start, a finish and three tricky turns. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Move the ball through with one finger. Notice where it is too easy or gets stuck. Tap Next when you’re ready.
Change two parts of the maze. Try to make it tricky but possible. Tap Next when you’re ready.

Ask someone to test it. Watch where they struggle, then improve one clue or turn. Show your maze and explain how your tester helped you improve it When you’re ready, show someone what you made or decided.
What did you learn when someone else tried your maze? You can tell me your idea, or show someone beside you. If it needs another go, that’s what inventors do.
